chunks: From him, from Fadala, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who borrows money, which is then lost or stolen; is there liability (guarantee) on the borrower? He said, 'There is no compensation/liability on him after the man has been trustworthy (in safeguarding it).'
ai.seo_question: Is the borrower liable to repay borrowed money if it is lost or stolen?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter of *Al-Ariyyah* (borrowing for use), this hadith clarifies the liability (*daman*) of a borrower who uses borrowed money (*istibda'*). It establishes that if the borrower is deemed *amin* (trustworthy and diligent), they are exempt from compensation if the funds are lost or stolen without their negligence, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that risk of loss falls on the owner unless fault is proven.
